examples.title: Index and search a small text-file corpus
examples.expected: three persisted documents; two Lucene matches
examples.adaptation: Uses three bundled text files and idempotent path updates instead of traversing an arbitrary directory.

examples.title: Search titles and contents separately
examples.expected: only id 1

examples.title: Exact identifiers versus analyzed text
examples.expected: exact SKU preserves case; analyzed text contains token abc

examples.title: Exact phrase search
examples.expected: matching ids 1

examples.title: Phrase proximity with slop
examples.expected: matching ids 1, 2

examples.title: Boolean MUST, FILTER and MUST_NOT clauses
examples.expected: only id 1

examples.title: Single-character wildcard and direct prefix queries
examples.expected: matching ids 1, 2

examples.title: One-edit typo tolerance
examples.expected: matching ids 1, 2
examples.adaptation: Uses current integer edit-distance syntax, not the obsolete fractional similarity syntax in older tutorials.

examples.title: Regular-expression terms
examples.expected: matching ids 1, 2

examples.title: Lexical date ranges on keyword fields
examples.expected: inclusive range finds two; exclusive range finds one

examples.title: Numeric point ranges for prices
examples.expected: only mid; text range syntax does not query LongPoint data

examples.title: Boost one term to change ranking
examples.expected: matching ids 1, 2

examples.title: English stemming and stop words
examples.expected: run matches both documents and the is removed
examples.adaptation: Uses built-in EnglishAnalyzer; its pipeline is not an exact copy of the historical custom Porter filter ordering.

examples.title: Inspect terms, positions and offsets
examples.expected: hello at 0..5 and lucene at 7..13

examples.title: Compare standard, whitespace and keyword analyzers
examples.expected: three distinct tokenization policies

examples.title: Read stored term frequencies, positions and offsets
examples.expected: red frequency 2 at positions 0 and 2; blue frequency 1

examples.title: Repeated fields, stored-only data and absent values
examples.expected: one hit with tag array [java, search]

examples.title: Update by ID and delete by exact term
examples.expected: one updated document, then zero live documents

examples.title: Near-real-time readers are immutable snapshots
examples.expected: old reader sees 1; new reader sees 2 without commit

examples.title: Explicit commit survives later rollback
examples.expected: only committed document remains

examples.title: Paginate scores with searchAfter
examples.expected: pages of 2, 2, 1; all five IDs exactly once
examples.adaptation: Uses a score cursor instead of the older demo’s overfetch-and-slice pagination; keep query, searcher and similarity unchanged.

examples.title: Sort results by numeric doc values
examples.expected: low first ascending; high first descending

examples.title: Sort results by keyword doc values
examples.expected: apple, mango, zebra

examples.title: Count author facets across all or matching documents
examples.expected: global Ada=2, Ben=1; query-relative Ada=1, Ben=1
examples.adaptation: Uses Lucene’s sorted-set doc-values facets, avoiding a separate taxonomy index.

examples.title: Filter by a facet and recalculate counts
examples.expected: two 2026 documents; refining author Ada leaves id 3
examples.adaptation: Adapts flat author/year drilldown; taxonomy hierarchies and DrillSideways are not exposed.

examples.title: Count multiple tags without double-counting documents
examples.expected: java=1, search=2; two documents in the dimension

examples.title: Nearest-neighbor search over explicit float vectors
examples.expected: near then middle, using Euclidean similarity
examples.adaptation: Uses explicit 2D fixture vectors; no embedding model, downloads or claim of semantic text understanding.

examples.title: Apply an eligibility filter inside KNN retrieval
examples.expected: near then far; excludes private middle

examples.title: Override analysis with a domain vocabulary rule
examples.expected: both spellings match; emitted tokens are car and color
examples.adaptation: Uses lmcode SAM entry dispatch from a Java TokenFilter instead of PyLucene’s PythonAnalyzer subclass.

examples.title: Use a field-statistics SAM rule to change ranking
examples.expected: baseline favors body; SAM weighting ranks title first

examples.title: Inspect BM25 length normalization and explanations
examples.expected: short text wins by default; b=0 produces equal scores

examples.title: Search a miniature manual-page catalog
examples.expected: find(1), with stored description
examples.adaptation: Uses a bundled three-record catalog; does not require or crawl the machine’s man-page installation.
